proto_cardiovascular_warning.message: Cardiovascular warning: measure again at rest.

recommendations.text: Rest for 5 minutes sitting down and measure again
Avoid intense effort until you get a normal reading
Write down any chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath and tell the medical officer

proto_cardiovascular_critical.message: Cardiovascular critical: tell someone now and do not stay alone.

recommendations.text: Tell someone who is with you right now and ask for help with the SOS button
Stop what you are doing, sit down and avoid any effort
Measure again after 5 minutes and log the value

proto_musculoskeletal_warning.message: Musculoskeletal warning: you have done less exercise than recommended today.

recommendations.text: Set aside a block today to complete your exercise session
If a long session does not fit, split it into two shorter blocks

proto_musculoskeletal_critical.message: Musculoskeletal critical: almost no exercise, and without it you lose bone and muscle.

recommendations.text: Resume your resistance exercise session as soon as you can
If you are not training because of pain or an injury, do not push yourself and tell the medical officer

proto_immune_warning.message: Immune warning: temperature outside the normal range.

recommendations.text: Take your temperature again in 30 minutes
Drink fluids and rest
Until you know whether it is an infection, limit close contact with others

proto_immune_critical.message: Immune critical: temperature very high or very low. Tell someone now.

recommendations.text: Tell the medical officer now and do not stay alone
Take your temperature again after 15 minutes and log the value

proto_metabolic_warning.message: Metabolic warning: glucose, hydration or weight outside the normal range.

recommendations.text: Measure again to confirm the value
Drink some water now and do not skip your next meal
If you notice shaking, cold sweats or dizziness, have something sugary and tell someone
Tell the medical officer now and do not stay alone
If your glucose is low, have some fast-acting sugar and measure again after 15 minutes
If it is due to a lack of fluids, drink water in small sips

proto_neuro_behavioral_warning.message: Neurobehavioral warning: sleep, mood or attention below your usual level.

recommendations.text: Make getting at least 7 hours of sleep tonight a priority
If you have slept little, avoid risky tasks or tasks that require a lot of attention today
Tell someone you trust how you are doing

proto_neuro_behavioral_critical.message: Neurobehavioral critical: do not carry this alone, ask for support today.

recommendations.text: Talk today with someone you trust or with the medical officer
Do not do critical tasks on your own until you feel better
If you prefer a confidential channel, use “I need to talk” in “Send alert to control”

proto_eyes_warning.message: Eyes warning: you have noticed changes in your vision.

recommendations.text: Note what you notice (blurred vision, blind spots, headache) and in which eye
Do the self-assessment again tomorrow at the same time
Mention it to the medical officer at your next consultation

proto_eyes_critical.message: Eyes critical: a sharp change in your vision. Tell someone now.

recommendations.text: Tell the medical officer now
Avoid tasks that depend on fine vision until you have been assessed

proto_radiation_warning.message: Radiation warning: your accumulated dose is above half of the career limit.

recommendations.text: Review the planning of your outside excursions with the medical officer
During a solar storm, stay in the most shielded area of the habitat

proto_radiation_critical.message: Radiation critical: the career dose limit has been reached.

recommendations.text: Tell the medical officer: your exposure needs to be replanned
Avoid any additional exposure that is not essential

proto_no_contact.message: No contact: someone needs to go and check on them.
steps: Call them by voice, radio or phone
Go to where they were last seen; if you can, take someone with you
When you find them, check whether they respond and are breathing normally
If they respond, ask them to confirm “I’m OK” on their device
If they do not respond or are not breathing normally, call for emergency help and start the first aid you are trained in
Note what you found in the alert and resolve it once they are safe
